chunks: Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Qutaybah al-A'sha, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'You have been antagonistic towards us regarding your fathers, and your sons, and your wives, and your reward is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, the time when you will be most in need [of us] is when the souls reach to here,' and he (peace be upon him) gestured with his hand to his throat.

key_terms.أَحْوَجَ مَا تَكُونُونَ: The most needed you will be

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Imam gesturing to his throat in this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) critiques the common practice of prioritizing familial bonds over loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt, warning that while the ultimate recompense lies with Allah, the spiritual peril is acute. The gesture to the throat signifies that this neglect becomes most critical at the moment of death, when the soul is seized and the need for divine intercession is paramount. This highlights the Shia concept of *Wala'* (loyalty) as a decisive factor in one's final spiritual state.
